thread:
ethan_sec: Noticing intermittent handshake failures (~1.8k rejects) from eu-central to svc-payments over the last hour. Pattern looks like client cert CN mismatch. Possibly related to yesterday's RBAC consolidation.

sofia_sre: Can you paste a log sample? Also check KMS decrypt audit for keystore-payments-eu.

ethan_sec: Paste from ingress: 
```
2026-03-25T09:07:12Z ingress-euc-3 svc-payments="svc-payments-01" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-payments-legacy, expected svc-payments)
2026-03-25T09:07:15Z ingress-euc-1 svc-payments="svc-payments-02" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-payments-legacy, expected svc-payments)
```

harper_infra: FYI we ran infra RBAC consolidation PR #4120 last night. It moved keystore access from individual service accounts to group:infra-ops. Might have left legacy project bindings around.

jules_dev: Rotator runs nightly at 03:30 UTC. rotator-bot should be the only principal hitting KMS. If legacy SA still bound, old certs could be minted during a staggered rollout.

sofia_sre: Pulled KMS audit for key "keystore-payments-eu" around 03:20-03:40Z:
```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-25T03:31:05Z","principal":"svc-payments-legacy@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":".../keystore-payments-key"}
{"timestamp":"2026-03-25T03:31:07Z","principal":"rotator-sa@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":".../keystore-payments-key"}
```

ethan_sec: So legacy SA still had decrypt access during rotation. That would explain CN mismatch. Did terraform forget to remove the binding?

harper_infra: Looks like terraform state has an orphan rule: `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.legacy_sa` still present in state file. There was a manual emergency change months ago that wasn't reconciled.

jules_dev: Quick mitigation suggestion: 1) remove legacy IAM binding for KMS (harper), 2) run a canary rotation (rotator with rotator-sa) targeting keystore-payments-eu, 3) run a small traffic canary and verify CNs, 4) create alert for any KMS decrypt by principals outside `rotator-sa` and `infra-ops` group.

sofia_sre: I'll remove the binding now and patch the monitoring rule. Notifying here when complete.

rotator-bot: rotator: scheduled rotation job keystore-payments-eu-20260325-canary at 2026-03-25T03:33:00Z using rotator-sa@infra.redwood

sofia_sre: Legacy binding removed @2026-03-25T03:35:12Z. Verified IAM policy no longer lists svc-payments-legacy.

rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation completed at 2026-03-25T03:36:40Z. New certs issued with CN=svc-payments.

jules_dev: Performed tls verification from eu-central probe: `openssl s_client -connect svc-payments.euc.internal:443` shows server accepted client certs signed to CN=svc-payments. Handshakes success.

ethan_sec: Reject rate back to baseline since 03:37Z. Root cause = leftover IAM binding for legacy service account after RBAC consolidation. Contributing factor = no alerting on KMS decrypt by unexpected principals.

harper_infra: I'll open an infra PR to remove the orphan state entry and add a terraform plan check to prevent drift. Will also add a small test that verifies keystore IAM matches expected list after apply.

sofia_sre: I've added an alert rule: if any decrypt on keystore-* keys occurs by a principal not in allowed_principals list, page sec-oncall. Also adding a weekly audit job that summarizes decrypt principals across regions.

jules_dev: Suggestion for long-term: rotator should validate the current IAM policy before rotation and optionally block if unexpected principals exist. Filed RFC draft.

ethan_sec: Thanks all. We'll track as P2 incident and include mitigation steps in the security tracker. If other regions show similar anomalies, we'll run the same checklist. :thumbsup:
